So `power start` uses `mag.power.start_all` (the full stack: backend + dashboard + mirror), while `wake` uses `mag.process_supervisor.start_all` (supervisor loops) + state brief. These are two different supervisor mechanisms. Let me check `mag.power.start_all` to understand the relationship and which is canonical.

Now I understand the architecture clearly: - **`power start`** (used by `mag_on.cmd`, `boot_mag.cmd`, `start_everything.cmd`) → spawns `mag_launch.py` supervisor (backend + dash + lab + scribe) + UI face. This is the full-stack turn-on. - **`wake`** → `process_supervisor.start_all()` (supervisor loops) + writes `state/START_BRIEF.md`. This is the "cheap cold start" that brings up the supervisor and gives the operator a measured brief. The task explicitly says `wake` is THE single documented entry. So `wake` is the canonical one-command. `power start`/`mag_launch.py` is the underlying full-stac

Now I have a complete understanding. `wake` starts the supervisor loops (autorun + ghost-daemon) and writes the START_BRIEF. Both verifications pass: - `operator_inbox.py` compiles and the ghost fix is correctly applied (ghost in system-source list, startswith branch removed). - RUN.md covers all 33 launchers. Let me do a final verification that the RUN.md renders correctly and check the README pointer is in place.
